correctness.rationale: The half-turn two-cycle is exact, and its return matrix has trace 1+λ²−t² and determinant λ². The strict Schur conditions give precisely 0<t<t_c and at equality the simple roots −1,−λ². For local uniqueness without assuming symmetry of an arbitrary candidate, use the odd return G=F² in a chart around the first phase. For any small G-two-cycle with points m±h its midpoint satisfies G(m+h)+G(m−h)−2m=0. The derivative in m at the critical origin is 2(DG−I), invertible; oddness gives m=0 as the unique local solution, so every such cycle satisfies G(p)=−p. The two one-step angular increments then force the displayed momenta and the two sine equations. Their Jacobian has complementary eigenvalue 2t_c and null vector w=(b,t_c+a). Eliminating the complementary coordinate and dividing the odd scalar equation by s reduces it to a smooth equation in s² with nonzero derivative −t_c k²(w_1^4+w_2^4)/6. Its root is s²=6μ/[k²(t_c²+a²)(t_c+a)]+O(μ²). The two signs correspond to one geometric prime four-cycle, and the negative side has no real nonzero root. In the trace of the two-step derivative at that branch, the change from the old cycle's trace is k²[t_c²(u²+v²)+a t_c(v²−u²)]/2+O(μ²)=6t_c μ+O(μ²); the net change from critical is 4t_c μ. The second two-step derivative is identical by oddness. Squaring the two eigenvalues gives 1−8t_c μ/(1−λ²)+O(μ²) and λ⁴+O(μ), both inside the unit disk for small μ>0. Independent scalar bisection and multiplication of four one-step Jacobians corroborated the amplitude and slope in nine cases.
residual_risks: The local estimates are for each fixed 0<λ<1; the small neighbourhood and error bounds need not be uniform near λ=1. Numeric checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: The exact resonant orbit is singled out by the half-turn drift and the sine zeros, rather than by an arbitrary numerical slice. Its stability boundary and the explicit supercritical branch give a local benchmark for the torqued dissipative standard map, including the dependence of the rate of attraction on damping. The full-space multiplier law and local uniqueness add more than merely identifying a generic flip.
residual_risks: No global bifurcation, basin classification or limit as damping vanishes is supported.
